inspiration.observed_pattern: A MySQL loader uses REGEXP_SUBSTR to extract the first matching token and, in other calls, supplies explicit start-position and occurrence controls.
inspiration.mysql_mariadb_translation: MariaDB 10.11.7 rejects the MySQL four-argument occurrence form with error 1582, so the independently authored case retains the compatible two-argument first-match extraction. It preserves NULL for missing input or a missing match without copying the source procedure, schema, or values.

fixture_notes: Note 101's first token is INC-482; note 102's first token is INC-305; note 103 is NULL; note 104's first token is INC-111. REGEXP_SUBSTR must preserve NULL for the absent input.
determinism_notes: All note IDs and text values are fixed; output is ordered by the unique note ID. No clocks, randomness, sleeps, or concurrent connections are used.
setup: CREATE TABLE incident_reference_lines (line_id INT PRIMARY KEY, line_text VARCHAR(128) NULL)
INSERT INTO incident_reference_lines VALUES (101, 'Escalated from INC-482 to INC-719'), (102, 'Only INC-305 appears'), (103, NULL), (104, 'INC-111 and INC-222')

steps.sql: SELECT line_id, REGEXP_SUBSTR(line_text, 'INC-[0-9]+') AS first_incident FROM incident_reference_lines ORDER BY line_id
